newsitem.title: USA: Oil slick investigation keeps tankers in Alaska.
newsitem.headline: Oil slick investigation keeps tankers in Alaska.

text.p: Oil tankers remained in Alaska's Port of Valdez Tuesday as harbor officials investigated the cause of an oil slick spotted Friday, oil companies and traders said.

The U.S. Coast Guard flew over the port at 1000 a.m. Alaska time (1400 EST/1900 GMT) to check the sheen's progress, said a spokeswoman for Alyeska Pipeline Service Co., a consortium which operates Alaska's 800-mile (1,280 km) pipeline into Valdez.
Coast Guard officials were trying to determine if a ballast-water-treatment plant leaked the oil, traders and officials said.
The investigation kept the plant shut, preventing at least two oil tankers from unloading their ballast water and leaving the port with full cargoes of Alaska crude oil , traders aid..
"We don't have a definite time as to when (the plant) is back up," said an Alyeska official.
Traders said two tankers operated by Atlantic Richfield Co. and BP America waited for the plant to re-open.
Both companies supply Alaskan crude oil to Californian and other West Coast refineries.
"We don't expect any of our shipments to be delayed at this time, but it is affecting us," said a trader whose company operates one of the ships.
Traders declined to comment on the ships' size and Coast Guard officials were not immediately available for comment.
Another trader said he expected the treatment plant to re-open Tuesday, but said the ships would leave the port partially loaded if necessary.
"Obviously, people would sail out with part cargoes," he said.
